title: Protected Disclosures — Organisational Receiving Process Flow
subtitle: Protected Disclosures Act 26 of 2000 (as amended 2017) and the Protected Disclosures Bill, 2026 · As at 19 October 2026

overview.summary: This flow tells a receiving organisation what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment a disclosure arrives until the case closes and lessons feed back into controls. It is built to comply with the law in force today and to be ready for the Bill without redesign.

notes.heading: Legal status
notes.text: The Protected Disclosures Act 26 of 2000, as amended by Act 5 of 2017 (“PDA”), is the binding law. The Protected Disclosures Bill, 2026 (“Bill”) was published for comment (closing 14 May 2026) and is not in force; it will repeal the PDA entirely (Bill s.32 and Schedule). Section numbers change completely between the two instruments. As at 19 October 2026 no report of Cabinet approval for tabling or introduction in Parliament was found, and a reported “revised” Bill text could not be located; re-check before this flow is adopted (verify).

notes.heading: Labels used throughout
points: PDA = binding now.

Bill = proposed; build readiness, do not treat as a current legal duty. Bill tests (e.g. the s.5 exclusions) never decide whether a disclosure is protected today; they are recorded as DRAFT readiness notes only.
BP = best practice or internal control; not a statutory deadline. Adopt as policy so it becomes binding internally.

notes.heading: Design principle
notes.text: Where the PDA and Bill differ, the flow applies the stricter of the two as internal policy. Running to Bill timelines now keeps the organisation comfortably inside the PDA and removes the need for a second redesign at commencement.

notes.heading: Five interpretation points that shape the flow
points: Counting days. Neither instrument says business or calendar days. Under the Interpretation Act 33 of 1957 s.4, “days” are calendar days, excluding the first day and including the last, unless the last day is a Sunday or public holiday. Diarise in calendar days.

Bill s.14 and the employer channel. Bill s.14(1) (5-day acknowledgement) applies to disclosures “made in terms of section 11”, which covers authorised persons other than the employer. Bill s.14(2) and the 12-month limit in s.14(8) apply to recipients in s.4(b)–(e), again excluding the employer. The employer’s own procedure is governed by s.12(5), which requires the employer to set its own time frames. However, s.14(3)–(7) refer to any “authorised person”, which by definition includes the employer. Treat all of s.14 as applying to the employer channel as a matter of policy.

The 10-day decision. Bill s.14(4) says the decision must be made “within 10 days” after the preliminary investigation, not “within 10 days of receipt”. Read literally, the outer limit is day 15. Plan for day 10 from receipt; treat day 15 as the absolute backstop.

Which PDA duties bind an employer. PDA s.3B (inserted in 2017) binds an employer receiving a disclosure under PDA s.6, as well as recipients under s.7 and s.8. Within 21 days it must decide whether to investigate, refer or not investigate, and acknowledge receipt in writing by informing the discloser of that decision. If it cannot decide within 21 days, it must say the decision is pending, update at intervals of not more than 2 months, and decide within 6 months. The “2 months” and “6 months” therefore relate to the pending decision, not to investigation progress or the final outcome. On conclusion of an investigation the recipient must also inform the discloser of the outcome (s.3B(4)). The duties to notify do not apply where the discloser’s identity and contact details are unknown (s.3B(5)(a)), and the notice duties in s.3B(1)(b), (2)(b) and (3) do not apply where compliance would prejudice the prevention, detection or investigation of a crime (s.3B(5)(b)). Where another recipient refers a disclosure to the organisation, the same 21-day duty runs from the referral (s.3B(2)).

Group structures. Where the organisation is a shareholder, parent or client that receives a disclosure about another entity, it may be the employer (PDA s.1 “employer” includes persons acting on the employer’s behalf; Bill s.6 adds clients) or a general recipient (PDA s.9 / Bill s.10). A disclosure referred in by another recipient runs the PDA s.3B(2) clock (step 1.1A). Confirm the recipient’s capacity at intake, because it decides which timelines and duties apply.

notes.heading: Roles used
notes.text: Designated Officer (DO); Legal Adviser (LA); HR Manager (HR); Appointed Investigator (INV); Database Manager (DBM); Senior Sign-off (SSO, e.g. CEO, CFO or Audit Committee chair where management is implicated); Board / Audit or Social & Ethics Committee (BOARD).

roles.name: Board / Audit or Social & Ethics Committee

stages.title: Phase 0 — Readiness (standing obligations)
intro: Phase 0 has no case trigger: it must be complete before the first disclosure arrives, because a discloser is only bound to use the internal procedure if the employer has made them aware of it (PDA s.6(1)(a) read with s.6(2)(a)(ii); Bill s.12(2)). Every later deadline assumes these controls exist.

notes.heading: Discloser side of Phase 0
notes.text: Nothing is owed by the discloser yet, but their later obligations depend on this phase: if the organisation has not communicated its procedure, the discloser may go straight to another authorised person and is deemed to have disclosed to the employer (PDA s.6(1)(b), s.6(2)(b); Bill s.12(3)–(4)).

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: A procedure that exists on paper but was never communicated gives the employer no benefit under PDA s.6(1)(a) read with s.6(2)(a)(ii) (Bill s.12(2)). Keep dated proof of communication for every worker category, including contractors.

steps.title: Adopt the procedure
steps.action: Board-approved policy and procedure covering every s.12(5) element: named DO and contact details; receipt and handling with time frames; onward referral; compulsory SAPS referral; review and investigation; handling of other wrongdoing found; anonymous reporting and confidentiality; outcome communication. Cover the full protected population, including contractors, TES workers, volunteers, trainees and related persons.

steps.title: Appoint the Designated Officer
steps.action: Name a DO and at least one alternate. Create an independent route (e.g. Audit Committee chair or external provider) for disclosures implicating the DO, CEO or executive.

steps.title: Communicate the procedure
steps.action: Bring the procedure to the attention of every employee and worker: induction, intranet, notice boards, contractor onboarding. Keep proof of communication.

steps.title: Stand up channels
steps.action: Written, electronic, oral and anonymous channels, with a return route for anonymous disclosers (case number lookup). If a hotline provider is used, sign an operator agreement covering confidentiality and security.

steps.title: Clean up contracts
steps.action: Remove or disapply clauses that exclude the Act or discourage disclosure: NDAs, settlement and exit agreements, supplier contracts. Such clauses are void.

steps.title: Publish website content
steps.action: Publish the five required items: what a protected disclosure is; how to make one; recipient contact details; remedies and protection procedures; when confidentiality-breach liability is excluded.

steps.deadline: Bill: on commencement (BP: now). Public and state-owned companies: see 0.6A (now)

steps.label: 0.6A
steps.title: Companies Act confidential disclosure system
steps.action: Public and state-owned companies: maintain the confidential disclosure system required by Companies Act s.159(7) and post the reg 131 notice of it, with contact details, at the registered office, main business premises and workplaces, on any website aimed at s.159(4) persons, and on the exchange news service if listed. s.159 also protects shareholders, directors, suppliers and other non-employees, so the channel must accept them.

steps.title: Prepare database registration
steps.action: Designate a Database Manager and alternate; draft a field map proving no discloser personal information will be uploaded. Register once the DoJ database and regulations are live.

steps.title: Case system and records
steps.action: Restricted-access case management, a separate sealed identity register, an evidence store with audit trail, and a POPIA retention schedule. Record the lawful basis for processing allegations of criminal behaviour (POPIA ss.26–27, 33) and any reliance on s.18(4) notification exceptions; route access requests by implicated persons to LA.

steps.title: Pre-agree external panel
steps.action: Pre-vet forensic investigators, external counsel, law enforcement contacts (SAPS, DPCI, IDAC), EAP and security support, so no time is lost in the 5- and 10-day windows.

steps.title: Train and raise awareness
steps.action: Train DO, HR, LA, investigators and line managers, including personal criminal exposure under the Bill. Train managers to forward any disclosure to the DO the same day.

stages.title: Phase 1 — Receipt and intake
intro: The clock starts on the day information about improper conduct reaches anyone who can receive it for the organisation, not when the DO first reads it. Day 0 is the day of receipt; day 1 is the next calendar day.

notes.heading: Discloser obligations at this stage
notes.text: Disclose in good faith, on reason to believe, to a qualifying recipient (PDA s.1 “disclosure”, ss.5–9; Bill s.4, s.5(a) DRAFT). Use the employer’s procedure if made aware of it (PDA s.6(1)(a); Bill s.12(2)). Provide the prescribed information in the prescribed manner (Bill s.11(1)). Sign the written record of an oral disclosure, or confirm agreement and affix a mark (Bill s.11(3)). Do not disclose information known to be false (PDA s.9B; Bill s.5(d), s.13).

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: Hotline operator → DO (same day). Line manager → DO (same day). IT → evidence preservation. Emergency services or SAPS where danger is imminent. DBM → DoJ database (Bill).

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: For an anonymous disclosure with no return route, record that acknowledgement was impossible and why. Do not open a separate grievance file and let the disclosure clock lapse: if a grievance and an allegation are mixed, run both in parallel.

steps.title: Recognise and forward
steps.trigger: Any person conveys information (not only opinion) about possible improper conduct, through any channel, including a line manager, a meeting remark or a hotline call. (PDA disclosures are made by an employee or worker, s.1; others are handled under Companies Act s.159 or as policy.)
steps.action: Recipient passes it to the DO without comment or investigation. Wrong internal recipient does not defeat protection: fix the channel administratively.
points: Recipient passes it to the DO without comment or investigation.
Wrong internal recipient does not defeat protection: fix the channel administratively.

steps.label: 1.1A
steps.title: Inbound referral
steps.trigger: Disclosure referred to us by another recipient (e.g. group parent, regulator or other s.6–8 recipient).
steps.action: Treat as a new matter from step 1.2. Day 0 = date the referral is received; the PDA s.3B(2) 21-day decision and notice duty applies, with pending notices and the 6-month backstop under s.3B(3) running from the referral.

steps.title: Log and reference
steps.action: Open case file; assign an identity-neutral reference; record date, time, channel, recipient and a verbatim or near-verbatim account. Record the discloser category (employee / worker per PDA s.1 / other) and whether Companies Act s.159 applies; this decides which statutory clocks run. Non-PDA disclosers are handled to the same standard as policy.

steps.title: Reduce oral disclosure to writing
steps.action: Write it up and have the discloser sign. If the discloser is illiterate or has a disability preventing a written disclosure: read aloud, interpret and explain in a language they understand, record their agreement and mark, and attach a certificate.

steps.deadline: At the intake meeting or within 2 days (BP)

steps.title: Secure identity
steps.action: Record identity only in the sealed identity register, separate from the case file. Everyone given access signs an undertaking. Release identity only with written consent and only to the extent consented to.

steps.title: Same-day danger and evidence screen
steps.trigger: Facts suggest imminent risk to life, health, safety or the environment, or evidence at risk of destruction.
steps.action: Escalate to emergency services, SAPS, or the OHS function as needed. Issue a litigation hold; image devices and email; restrict system access. Brief LA on a possible s.15 application.

steps.title: Acknowledge in writing
steps.trigger: Every disclosure where a return route exists, including anonymous disclosures via the channel.
steps.action: Send an acknowledgement: reference number; what happens next and when; single point of contact; confidentiality and its limits (court or law may require disclosure); summary of protection; request for any further information. Do not state whether it is protected yet. Before sending, LA to confirm whether PDA s.3B(5)(b) applies (notice would prejudice a criminal investigation, including FICA tipping-off). If so, withhold, record reasons on F09, and diarise when notice can safely be given. Where identity and contact details are unknown, s.3B(5)(a) applies: record it.

steps.deadline: Bill: within 5 days (s.14(1)); PDA: within 21 days, combined with the decision (s.3B(1))

steps.title: Database entry
steps.trigger: Bill in force and database live.
steps.action: Upload receipt and date of receipt, with no personal information of the discloser. Cross-reference the internal case number.

Cross-reference the internal case number.
steps.deadline: Bill: manner and timing to be prescribed; BP within 5 days

steps.title: Diarise all clocks
steps.action: Calendar, with owners: PDA day 21 (decision/acknowledgement or pending notice), pending notices at ≤ 2-month intervals and the 6-month decision backstop (binding now); and the Bill acknowledgement, preliminary-assessment, decision, 3-monthly update, 9-month review and 12-month deadlines (policy now).

stages.title: Phase 2 — Triage and preliminary assessment
intro: By day 5 (Bill s.14(3) timeline, adopted as policy) record a documented classification. Whether a disclosure is protected is decided only under the PDA in force: good faith (ss.6–8; s.9), reason to believe (s.1), a qualifying channel (ss.5–9) and, for s.8 and s.9 recipients, a reasonable belief that it is substantially true. Bill tests are recorded as DRAFT readiness notes and never ground a “not protected” decision. Protection work starts now and does not wait for that answer.

notes.heading: Discloser obligations at this stage
notes.text: Provide further information if asked, truthfully. Do not continue participating in the conduct disclosed; that is a revocation ground (Bill s.27(1)(a)). Do not commit an offence under the Act while providing information (s.27(1)(d)).

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: DO → LA (PDA protection test and route opinion). DO → independent route where conflicted. DO → police official / DPCI (PRECCA s.34) or FIC (FICA s.29) where triggered. HR → retaliation monitoring.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: Do not test whether the allegation is true at triage. Under the PDA, protection attaches to a disclosure made in good faith, on reason to believe, through a qualifying channel (ss.5–9); for s.8 and s.9 recipients the discloser must also reasonably believe it is substantially true. Truth is for Phase 4. Never classify a disclosure as “not protected” on Bill criteria: discipline that follows risks an automatically unfair dismissal (LRA s.187(1)(h)) or unfair labour practice (s.186(2)(d)) finding.

steps.title: Threshold test
steps.action: Is it information about improper conduct by an employer or employee: POCA or PRECCA offences, any crime, breach of a legal obligation, miscarriage of justice, health or safety danger, environmental damage, EEA or PEPUDA discrimination, or concealment of any of these? Location and governing law are irrelevant. A pure personal grievance goes to the grievance procedure with a redirect notice.

A pure personal grievance goes to the grievance procedure with a redirect notice.
steps.form: F07 memo, part A; F29 redirect

steps.title: Recipient capacity and route
steps.action: Confirm in what capacity the organisation received it: employer (PDA s.6 / Bill s.6), legal adviser (PDA s.5 / Bill s.7), Cabinet member or MEC (PDA s.7 / Bill s.8), Chapter 9 body, PSC, AG or prescribed body (PDA s.8 and GN R.949 / Bill s.9), or general recipient (PDA s.9 / Bill s.10). For a general disclosure record the s.9(1) beliefs, the s.9(2) trigger and the s.9(3) factors.

steps.title: Protection test (PDA)
steps.action: PDA test (binding): confirm the disclosure was made in good faith (PDA ss.6–8), on reason to believe it shows an impropriety (s.1), through a qualifying channel (ss.5–9), and, for s.8/s.9 recipients, on a reasonable belief that it is substantially true; for s.9 also confirm a s.9(2) trigger and s.9(3) reasonableness. Test on evidence, not tone or timing; mixed motives do not automatically defeat good faith. Get a written LA opinion before any “not protected” finding. Bill s.5 exclusions (wrong recipient, known or ought-to-have-known falsity, intent to harm, pecuniary gain, illegal purpose, avoiding discipline): record for readiness only; they do not decide protection today.

steps.title: Classification
steps.action: Record one of: protected under the PDA; not protected under the PDA (only on the step 2.3 PDA test, with LA opinion, never on Bill s.5 grounds); or grounds not to investigate (Bill s.14(5) grounds adopted as policy: no merit, trivial, more appropriate lawful method, or previously adequately dealt with). Note separately, as DRAFT readiness, whether the Bill tests would give a different result. A “not protected” finding removes statutory protection; it does not remove the need to deal with a credible allegation through ordinary governance, and it never justifies discipline for making the disclosure without separate LA advice (LRA s.187(1)(h), s.186(2)(d)).

steps.title: Mandatory-referral screen
steps.trigger: Any sign of crime, a parallel investigation, or imminent danger.
steps.action: Check: is another body already investigating (coordinate now, see 3.4; Bill s.14(9)(a)(i) stand-down on commencement)? Is a crime clearly committed (refer to law enforcement, s.14(9)(a)(ii))? Does the DO reasonably believe it is a crime or imminent danger (compulsory SAPS referral, s.12(5)(c))? Does PRECCA s.34 apply: does a person in a position of authority know, or suspect (or ought reasonably to know or suspect), that any corruption offence (PRECCA ss.3–16 or 20–21, any amount) or theft, fraud, extortion, forgery or uttering involving R100,000 or more has been committed? If so, report to a police official (SAPS/DPCI) and record the CAS number. Is a FICA s.29 report required, with tipping-off restrictions? If notice to the discloser would prejudice either, apply PDA s.3B(5)(b) (see 1.6).

steps.title: Conflict and escalation check
steps.trigger: DO, executive or board member implicated, or the organisation itself is the subject.
steps.action: Move the matter to the independent route. Record that a disclosure about the employer may not be referred back to that employer.
points: Move the matter to the independent route.

steps.title: Retaliation and related-person risk
steps.action: Map reporting lines, who controls the discloser’s pay, performance, shifts and contract renewals, and who else is exposed: family, household, colleagues, anyone who assisted. Put interim measures in place and record reasons at the time.

steps.title: Privilege and implicated persons
steps.action: LA to instruct any written analysis to preserve privilege. Treat the allegation as unproven; restrict circulation. Allegations of crime are special personal information (POPIA s.26): process only under an authorisation (ss.27, 33), document any s.18(4) notification exception, and route implicated persons’ access requests to LA. Any suspension of an implicated person must rest on the ordinary disciplinary policy, not on the disclosure.

stages.title: Phase 3 — Investigation decision
intro: The discloser must receive a written decision: under the Bill within 10 days after the preliminary investigation (plan for day 10; backstop day 15), and under the PDA within 21 days of the disclosure. Silence is itself a breach.

notes.heading: Discloser obligations at this stage
notes.text: None new. A discloser dissatisfied with a decline may disclose elsewhere; the organisation must not discourage this, and any contract term that tries to is void (PDA s.2(3); Bill s.11(4)).

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: DO → receiving authorised person (with a redacted pack). DO → law enforcement agency. DBM → database (referral date and recipient, or dismissal and reason). DO → Phase 4 investigator.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: The retired judge under Bill s.24 hears complaints about detrimental action, identity breaches, revocation and extension applications. It is not a forum for appealing a decision not to investigate, so do not signpost it as one.

steps.title: Decide the route
steps.action: Choose: investigate internally; refer to another authorised person; or not investigate on a s.14(5) ground. Senior sign-off; LA review of every decline.
points: Choose: investigate internally; refer to another authorised person; or not investigate on a s.14(5) ground.
Senior sign-off; LA review of every decline.
steps.deadline: Bill: 10 days after preliminary investigation; PDA: 21 days

steps.title: If PDA decision not possible
steps.trigger: Matter too complex to decide by day 21 (PDA).
steps.action: Tell the discloser in writing that a decision is pending; repeat at intervals of not more than 2 months; decide within 6 months.
points: Tell the discloser in writing that a decision is pending; repeat at intervals of not more than 2 months; decide within 6 months.
steps.deadline: PDA: day 21, then every ≤ 2 months, final by 6 months

steps.label: 3.3a
steps.title: Investigate
steps.action: Written notice: decision, who will investigate (role), update frequency, expected timeline. Proceed to Phase 4.
points: Written notice: decision, who will investigate (role), update frequency, expected timeline.
Proceed to Phase 4.

steps.label: 3.3b
steps.title: Refer to another authorised person
steps.action: Tell the discloser the reasons and which body; send the referral without identity unless the discloser has consented in writing; update the database. Never refer back to the employer that is the subject.
points: Tell the discloser the reasons and which body; send the referral without identity unless the discloser has consented in writing; update the database.
Never refer back to the employer that is the subject.
steps.deadline: With 3.1; database update BP within 5 days
steps.form: F09 variant B; F10 referral letter; F23
steps.authority: Bill s.14(4)(b), (7)(a)–(c), s.19(1); PDA s.3B(1)(a)(ii); attach PDA s.8 / GN R.949 list to F10

steps.label: 3.3c
steps.title: Not investigate
steps.action: Written reasons. Name the discloser’s real options: disclosure to a body listed in or prescribed under PDA s.8 (GN R.949 of 2018; attach the list to F09 variant C), or a general disclosure under PDA s.9(2)(c) if no action is taken within a reasonable period. (Bill, on commencement: s.9 bodies, s.10(2)(c) and court review.) Record the dismissal and reason on the database.
points: Written reasons.

Name the discloser’s real options: disclosure to a body listed in or prescribed under PDA s.8 (GN R.949 of 2018; attach the list to F09 variant C), or a general disclosure under PDA s.9(2)(c) if no action is taken within a reasonable period.
(Bill, on commencement: s.9 bodies, s.10(2)(c) and court review.) Record the dismissal and reason on the database.

steps.title: Coordinate with another body that is investigating
steps.trigger: Same subject already under investigation by a body authorised by law.
steps.action: PDA (now): do not duplicate the agency’s work; agree in writing with the agency which internal steps (including discipline) may proceed, and keep disciplinary capability. Inform the discloser in writing unless PDA s.3B(5)(b) applies (record reasons on F09). Bill (on commencement): stand down per s.14(9)(a).
points: PDA (now): do not duplicate the agency’s work; agree in writing with the agency which internal steps (including discipline) may proceed, and keep disciplinary capability.
Inform the discloser in writing unless PDA s.3B(5)(b) applies (record reasons on F09).
Bill (on commencement): stand down per s.14(9)(a).
steps.deadline: PDA: decision within 21 days; Bill: inform within 5 days of becoming aware (policy)
steps.authority: PDA s.3B(1)(a), s.3B(5)(b); Bill s.14(9)(a)(i), (b) (on commencement)

steps.title: Law enforcement referral
steps.trigger: Crime clearly committed, or DO reasonably believes crime or imminent danger.
steps.action: Refer to SAPS, DPCI, IDAC or the relevant agency with an evidence summary; record the case number. Where PRECCA s.34 applies (any corruption offence, or theft, fraud, extortion, forgery or uttering of R100,000+, known or suspected), report to a police official (SAPS/DPCI). Before informing the discloser, LA to confirm whether PDA s.3B(5)(b) applies; if so, withhold, record reasons on F09 and diarise when notice can safely be given. Agree with the agency how any internal disciplinary process will run without prejudicing the criminal case.
points: Refer to SAPS, DPCI, IDAC or the relevant agency with an evidence summary; record the case number.
Where PRECCA s.34 applies (any corruption offence, or theft, fraud, extortion, forgery or uttering of R100,000+, known or suspected), report to a police official (SAPS/DPCI).
Before informing the discloser, LA to confirm whether PDA s.3B(5)(b) applies; if so, withhold, record reasons on F09 and diarise when notice can safely be given.
Agree with the agency how any internal disciplinary process will run without prejudicing the criminal case.
steps.deadline: Imminent danger: immediately; inform discloser within 5 days of becoming aware; BP: refer within 5 days
steps.authority: PRECCA s.34; PDA s.3B(5)(b); Bill s.12(5)(c), s.14(9)(a)(ii), (b) (DRAFT)

stages.title: Phase 4 — Investigation
intro: Under the Bill the investigation must finish within 12 months of receipt, with one extension of up to 6 months granted by the retired judge (Bill s.14(8)). The PDA sets no outer limit; adopt the Bill’s limit as policy.

notes.heading: Discloser obligations at this stage
notes.text: Cooperate truthfully; keep the investigation’s confidential information confidential except where a court or law requires it (Bill s.19(3)(a)). Do not continue participating in the conduct.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: DO → external investigator. LA → High Court or magistrate’s court (s.15). DO → retired judge (extension). HR → independent approver. Investigator → law enforcement if a crime becomes clear mid-investigation (coordinate now; stand down under Bill s.14(9) on commencement).

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: The update record is evidence in its own right: a missed 3-monthly update breaches internal policy now and will be a statutory breach once the Bill commences. Calendar every update on day 0.

steps.title: Appoint investigator
steps.action: Appoint someone free of any reporting line, financial interest or relationship with implicated persons. External appointment, instructed by LA and overseen by the Board, where senior management is implicated. Signed conflict declaration, undertaking and terms of reference.
points: Appoint someone free of any reporting line, financial interest or relationship with implicated persons.
External appointment, instructed by LA and overseen by the Board, where senior management is implicated.
Signed conflict declaration, undertaking and terms of reference.

steps.title: Plan and brief
steps.action: Investigation plan with milestones; brief the investigator that concealing or suppressing evidence is an offence (up to 15 years).
points: Investigation plan with milestones; brief the investigator that concealing or suppressing evidence is an offence (up to 15 years).

steps.title: Gather evidence
steps.action: Collect documents and data under chain of custody; interview witnesses after a confidentiality briefing; give implicated persons a fair opportunity to respond. Where another form of wrongdoing emerges, extend scope under the procedure.
points: Collect documents and data under chain of custody; interview witnesses after a confidentiality briefing; give implicated persons a fair opportunity to respond.
Where another form of wrongdoing emerges, extend scope under the procedure.
steps.authority: Bill s.12(5)(d)–(e); PAJA (public bodies); audi alteram partem

steps.title: Court assistance
steps.trigger: Evidence likely to be destroyed, concealed or tampered with, or a witness under pressure, inducement or intimidation.
steps.action: Apply to court for a preservation or restraint order. This is a duty, not a discretion. If the risk is assessed as below threshold, record why.
points: Apply to court for a preservation or restraint order.
This is a duty, not a discretion.
If the risk is assessed as below threshold, record why.

steps.title: Progress updates
steps.action: Written, substantive update: steps done, steps outstanding, next update date. Anonymous disclosers via the return channel.
points: Written, substantive update: steps done, steps outstanding, next update date.
Anonymous disclosers via the return channel.

steps.title: Extension
steps.trigger: Month-9 review shows the 12-month limit is at risk.
steps.action: Apply to the retired judge in the prescribed manner for up to 6 more months, before the 12 months expire. Only one extension is possible. Tell the discloser.
points: Apply to the retired judge in the prescribed manner for up to 6 more months, before the 12 months expire.
Only one extension is possible.
Tell the discloser.
steps.deadline: Apply by month 10 (BP); limit is month 12

steps.title: Adverse-action review
steps.trigger: Any proposed HR decision affecting the discloser or a related person: discipline, performance rating, transfer, contract renewal, promotion.
steps.action: Independent approver reviews before it is taken; reasons recorded separately from the disclosure file, showing the decision is not linked to the disclosure.
points: Independent approver reviews before it is taken; reasons recorded separately from the disclosure file, showing the decision is not linked to the disclosure.

steps.title: Parallel discipline
steps.trigger: Disciplinary process against the discloser pre-dates or runs alongside.
steps.action: Keep it structurally separate, with its own chairperson and file. Document the chronology showing independent grounds.
points: Keep it structurally separate, with its own chairperson and file.
Document the chronology showing independent grounds.

steps.title: Transfer request
steps.trigger: Discloser reasonably believes they may be adversely affected and asks to move.
steps.action: Transfer if reasonably possible or practicable, on terms no less favourable without written consent.
points: Transfer if reasonably possible or practicable, on terms no less favourable without written consent.

steps.title: Identity demands
steps.trigger: A court or law requires confidential information, or a complaint under s.24(3)(b)(ii) is lodged.
steps.action: Tell the discloser in advance where possible. If a complaint is lodged with the retired judge, disclose nothing until the judge’s investigation and recommendation are complete. Seek in camera evidence or redaction orders.
points: Tell the discloser in advance where possible.
If a complaint is lodged with the retired judge, disclose nothing until the judge’s investigation and recommendation are complete.
Seek in camera evidence or redaction orders.

steps.title: Revocation check
steps.trigger: Evidence that the discloser participated after disclosing, made a knowingly false material statement, disclosed solely or substantially to avoid discipline, or committed an Act offence.
steps.action: Stop; LA opinion; follow the revocation protocol in section 10. Protection continues while any challenge runs.
points: Stop; LA opinion; follow the revocation protocol in section 10.
Protection continues while any challenge runs.

stages.title: Phase 5 — Close, outcome and enforcement
intro: The case is closed only when the report is issued, the discloser has a substantive outcome, any crime is referred, and the database and records are finalised. Recommendations then carry High Court enforcement risk under the Bill.

notes.heading: Discloser obligations at this stage
notes.text: Keep the report’s confidential content confidential except as law or a court requires. A discloser aggrieved by the report may apply to court for review in the prescribed manner (Bill s.16(3)).

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: DO → discloser, employer or relevant person (report). DO → law enforcement. Management → BOARD (recommendation tracking). LA → High Court (s.17 enforcement, or defending one). DBM → database.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: “The matter is concluded” is not an outcome notice. Give enough substance for the discloser to understand the result and what they can still do.

steps.title: Report
steps.action: Report with findings and recommendations. Draft redacted from the first paragraph: no confidential personal information about the discloser, including indirect identifiers such as dates, quotes or org-chart detail.
points: Report with findings and recommendations.
Draft redacted from the first paragraph: no confidential personal information about the discloser, including indirect identifiers such as dates, quotes or org-chart detail.

steps.title: Distribute report
steps.action: Make available to the discloser; the discloser’s employer (or former employer at the time of the conduct); or the relevant person where the disclosure is not about an employer.
points: Make available to the discloser; the discloser’s employer (or former employer at the time of the conduct); or the relevant person where the disclosure is not about an employer.

steps.title: Outcome notice
steps.action: Substantive notice: what was found, what is being done, and the discloser’s remaining options (Bill, on commencement: court review of the report, s.16(3); complaint or court if detriment occurs). Withhold third-party personal information and live criminal-case detail. Not required only where the discloser’s identity and contact details are unknown (PDA s.3B(5)(a)).
points: Substantive notice: what was found, what is being done, and the discloser’s remaining options (Bill, on commencement: court review of the report, s.16(3); complaint or court if detriment occurs).
Withhold third-party personal information and live criminal-case detail.
Not required only where the discloser’s identity and contact details are unknown (PDA s.3B(5)(a)).
steps.authority: PDA s.3B(4) (statutory: inform discloser of outcome at conclusion); Bill s.16(2)–(3)

steps.title: Law enforcement referral
steps.action: Refer to the relevant agency regardless of any internal sanction; record the case number. PRECCA s.34 offences (any corruption offence, or theft, fraud, extortion, forgery or uttering of R100,000+) go to a police official (SAPS/DPCI).
points: Refer to the relevant agency regardless of any internal sanction; record the case number.
PRECCA s.34 offences (any corruption offence, or theft, fraud, extortion, forgery or uttering of R100,000+) go to a police official (SAPS/DPCI).

steps.title: Implement recommendations
steps.action: Owner and due date per recommendation; track to completion; report to BOARD. Unimplemented recommendations can be enforced in the High Court by the authorised person or any interested party.
points: Owner and due date per recommendation; track to completion; report to BOARD.
Unimplemented recommendations can be enforced in the High Court by the authorised person or any interested party.

steps.title: Finalise database
steps.action: Record finalisation and date.
points: Record finalisation and date.

steps.title: Records retention
steps.action: Keep records only as long as needed to finalise, unless law requires or lawful purposes reasonably require longer. If kept longer, record reasons without delay and tell the discloser. Destroy or de-identify per POPIA.
points: Keep records only as long as needed to finalise, unless law requires or lawful purposes reasonably require longer.
If kept longer, record reasons without delay and tell the discloser.
Destroy or de-identify per POPIA.

steps.title: Close protection file
steps.action: End-state retaliation assessment; set a post-closure watch period for adverse actions (BP 12 months), since retaliation often follows closure.
points: End-state retaliation assessment; set a post-closure watch period for adverse actions (BP 12 months), since retaliation often follows closure.

steps.title: Award readiness
steps.trigger: Organisation prosecuted and a monetary sanction possible.
steps.action: Preserve records of what information came from whom and when, since the court tests origin, novelty and proof of offence elements. Public servants, PRECCA s.34 reporters, plea-deal informants, accomplices and law enforcement officials are excluded.
points: Preserve records of what information came from whom and when, since the court tests origin, novelty and proof of offence elements.
Public servants, PRECCA s.34 reporters, plea-deal informants, accomplices and law enforcement officials are excluded.

stages.title: Phase 6 — Governance and learning
intro: Phase 6 turns individual cases into control improvements and board oversight. Almost none of it has a statutory deadline, so it must be fixed in policy or it will be skipped.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: DO → Audit / Social and Ethics Committee. Compliance → website owner. LA → policy owners.

steps.title: Root-cause review
steps.action: Which control failed; whether policy was adequate; whether internal channels were trusted; whether related persons were affected. Review the organisation, never the discloser’s credibility.
points: Which control failed; whether policy was adequate; whether internal channels were trusted; whether related persons were affected.
Review the organisation, never the discloser’s credibility.

steps.title: Governance reporting
steps.action: Volumes by channel and category; timeliness against every deadline; retaliation complaints; referrals; recommendations outstanding; policy changes. Aggregate only.
points: Volumes by channel and category; timeliness against every deadline; retaliation complaints; referrals; recommendations outstanding; policy changes.
Aggregate only.
steps.authority: King V Code on Corporate Governance (2025; effective for financial years from 1 Jan 2026), ethics and compliance principles (confirm principle number from the Code); Companies Regulations reg. 43 (Social and Ethics Committee, where applicable)

steps.title: External visibility check
steps.action: Anticipate that database data will appear in the DoJ Annual Report and complaints in the retired judge’s annual report. Reconcile internal figures with database entries.
points: Anticipate that database data will appear in the DoJ Annual Report and complaints in the retired judge’s annual report.
Reconcile internal figures with database entries.

steps.title: Policy and website refresh
steps.trigger: Annually, or on any change of DO, channel or law.
steps.action: Update procedure, DO contact details and the five s.29(4) website items; re-communicate.
points: Update procedure, DO contact details and the five s.29(4) website items; re-communicate.

steps.title: Training refresh
steps.action: Refresh DO, HR, LA, investigator and manager training, including the offences register in section 14.
points: Refresh DO, HR, LA, investigator and manager training, including the offences register in section 14.

steps.title: Legislative watch
steps.action: Track introduction in Parliament, amendments, commencement proclamation (which may differ per provision, s.33(2)) and regulations. Run a gap analysis at each step.
points: Track introduction in Parliament, amendments, commencement proclamation (which may differ per provision, s.33(2)) and regulations.
Run a gap analysis at each step.

stages.group: Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies
stages.title: Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies
intro: This track opens on day 0 and runs until the post-closure watch period ends. Its events are triggered by what happens to people, not by the case timeline.

steps.label: P1
steps.title: Confidentiality
steps.action: Identity and identifying information released only with written consent and to employees competent to deal with the disclosure; no investigation information to any other person.
points: Identity and identifying information released only with written consent and to employees competent to deal with the disclosure; no investigation information to any other person.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P2
steps.title: Liability shield
steps.trigger: Discloser threatened with a civil claim or charge for breaching confidentiality.
steps.action: Do not institute or threaten; such a threat is itself occupational detriment. LA to assess reasonable-belief test.
points: Do not institute or threaten; such a threat is itself occupational detriment.
LA to assess reasonable-belief test.
steps.authority: Bill s.20, s.1 “occupational detriment” (h)–(i); PDA s.9A

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P3
steps.title: Occupational detriment
steps.trigger: Any adverse employment action linked in any way to the disclosure.
steps.action: Prevent via 4.7; if it occurs, reverse and remedy. The employer, the person acting with its authority and a client are jointly and severally liable.
points: Prevent via 4.7; if it occurs, reverse and remedy.
The employer, the person acting with its authority and a client are jointly and severally liable.
steps.authority: Bill s.21(1), (7)–(8); PDA s.3, s.3A (joint and several liability of employer and client)

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P4
steps.title: Detrimental action
steps.trigger: Threats, intimidation, harassment, injury, property damage or discrimination against the discloser or any related person, inside or outside work.
steps.action: Security response; SAPS report where criminal; EAP support; record in F08. Protect against acts by third parties the organisation incites, authorises or knowingly permits.
points: Security response; SAPS report where criminal; EAP support; record in F08.
Protect against acts by third parties the organisation incites, authorises or knowingly permits.
steps.authority: Bill s.1 “detrimental action”, s.21(2)–(3), (8): up to 15 years

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P5
steps.title: Burden of proof
steps.trigger: Discloser shows a protected disclosure and a linked detriment.
steps.action: Organisation must show the action was not retaliatory; its evidence is the F18 record made at the time.
points: Organisation must show the action was not retaliatory; its evidence is the F18 record made at the time.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P6
steps.title: Witness protection
steps.action: Tell the discloser the Witness Protection Act applies and how to apply to the Office for Witness Protection; do not apply on their behalf without consent.
points: Tell the discloser the Witness Protection Act applies and how to apply to the Office for Witness Protection; do not apply on their behalf without consent.
steps.authority: Bill s.22; WPA s.7 as amended by Schedule

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P7
steps.title: Legal aid
steps.trigger: Discloser in court or tribunal and cannot afford representation.
steps.action: Court or tribunal refers to Legal Aid SA; organisation to respect confidentiality of that direction.
points: Court or tribunal refers to Legal Aid SA; organisation to respect confidentiality of that direction.
steps.authority: Bill s.23; Legal Aid SA Act s.22A (inserted)

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P8
steps.title: Complaint to retired judge
steps.trigger: Discloser, related person or representative complains of detrimental action, imminent identity disclosure or revocation.
steps.action: Respond to information requests (refusal without lawful ground is an offence); allow entry to premises for documents; give reasonable assistance; do not interfere. Receive the judge’s decision and any referral to law enforcement or a Chapter 9 institution.
points: Respond to information requests (refusal without lawful ground is an offence); allow entry to premises for documents; give reasonable assistance; do not interfere.
Receive the judge’s decision and any referral to law enforcement or a Chapter 9 institution.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P9
steps.title: Revocation
steps.trigger: Evidence of a s.27(1) ground during or after investigation.
steps.action: LA-signed written notice to the discloser; notify the Director: Office for Witness Protection if the person is under protection; signpost complaint or court. Protection continues until the judge or court rules otherwise if challenged.
points: LA-signed written notice to the discloser; notify the Director: Office for Witness Protection if the person is under protection; signpost complaint or court.
Protection continues until the judge or court rules otherwise if challenged.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — protection, complaints, revocation and remedies

steps.label: P10
steps.title: Remedies claimed
steps.trigger: Discloser or related person lodges a complaint, CCMA referral or Labour Court or other court claim.
steps.action: Litigation response. Dismissal in breach is automatically unfair; other detriment is an unfair labour practice via LRA s.191 conciliation, then Labour Court. Courts may order compensation, actual damages or remedial steps.
points: Litigation response.
Dismissal in breach is automatically unfair; other detriment is an unfair labour practice via LRA s.191 conciliation, then Labour Court.
Courts may order compensation, actual damages or remedial steps.
steps.deadline: Employee referral windows: 30 days (dismissal, from dismissal or, if later, the final decision to dismiss or uphold it) / 90 days (unfair labour practice, from the act or knowledge of it)

referenceTables.title: Master flow at a glance
intro: Every channel feeds one intake; Phase 3 branches into investigate or refer/decline, and both close in Phase 5. The protection track is not a phase: it opens on day 0 and runs until the case closes, whatever the triage outcome.

Read each phase column top to bottom to see who acts and who hands off; read each lane left to right to see one party’s whole job. The Designated Officer lane is the spine: every other lane connects to it, and the protection lane runs underneath from day 0 until the post-closure watch ends.

PDA “progress updates every 2 months” and “outcome within 6 months”

Under PDA s.3B these relate to a pending decision, not investigation progress or outcome. The PDA has no outcome deadline, but s.3B(4) does require the discloser to be told the outcome when the investigation concludes (statutory now).
PDA “acknowledge within 21 days” as a stand-alone step
PDA s.3B joins acknowledgement to informing the discloser of the decision within 21 days.
Decline letters signpost a complaint to the retired judge
Baseline 3.2, T4 variant C; Flow Table 3.2; slide 25

Bill s.24(3) covers detrimental action, identity breaches, revocation and extensions, not declines. Signpost PDA s.8 bodies (GN R.949 of 2018) and a general disclosure under PDA s.9(2)(c) instead; Bill s.9, s.10(2)(c) and court review only once the Bill commences.
Bill s.3 sets no timing; it will be prescribed. Label as BP pending regulations.
Bill s.14(1), (2) and (8) presented as binding employers
Textually these apply to s.11 and s.4(b)–(e) recipients, not the employer channel. Apply by policy and say so.
Training “now a statutory duty for both sectors” citing s.29(2)–(3)
s.29(2)–(3) bind Cabinet members and SAJEI. Employers’ duties are s.29(1) (awareness) and s.29(4) (website).
Investigator “within 10 days”, database close “within 5 days”, root cause “within 30 days” shown beside statutory citations
Internal BP only. Label clearly so they are not mistaken for law.
Framatome disclosure analysed under PDA s.8 and Bill s.9

Those sections list public oversight bodies. A majority shareholder is more likely an employer-side recipient (Bill s.6: client or person acting on behalf) or a general recipient (PDA s.9; Bill s.10). LA to review the opinion’s reasoning.
Acknowledgement row “failure risk: criminal offence to suppress evidence”
Mismatched; missing an acknowledgement is non-compliance, not the s.14(11) offence.
Cite King V (2025; effective for financial years from 1 January 2026) by name; confirm the principle number from the Code itself before citing.
PDA s.3B cited for investigation conduct and independence
s.3B deals with deciding and informing only.

intro: Scope mismatch in s.14: subsections (1), (2) and (8) exclude employers; (3)–(7) include them. The 12-month limit and extension regime should expressly apply, or not apply, to employers.
s.14(4) has a dangling “or” and an unclear starting point for the 10 days. “Days” is not defined as business or calendar days.

s.14(9)(a)(ii) bars any investigation where a crime is clearly committed. Read literally, this stops employers running internal forensic or disciplinary investigations into fraud. A coordination mechanism with law enforcement is needed instead.
s.12(5)(d) requires PAJA-compliant review by all employers, although PAJA governs administrative action by organs of state.
s.18(1) refers to convicting an employer “of improper conduct in terms of this Act”, but the Act creates no such offence.
s.21 has two subsections numbered (3), and s.21(3)(b) contains a stray “because”. s.19(3)(a) is double-lettered.
s.24(3)(a) refers to extension under s.14(8)(a); the extension provision is s.14(8)(b).
The Schedule’s amendments refer to the Protected Disclosures Act 2000 (and “Act No. 26 of 2025”) instead of the new Act, and its heading cites section 31 instead of 32.
There is no mechanism to challenge a decision not to investigate, and no time limit for issuing the s.16 report.
s.11(3) requires a signature on oral disclosures, which sits awkwardly with anonymous oral disclosures under s.11(2).
